ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a rectangle JKLM the angle bisector in $\mathrm{J}$ intersects the diagonal KM in $\mathrm{N}$. The distance of $\mathrm{N}$ to $\mathrm{LM}$ is 1 and the distance of $\mathrm{N}$ to $\mathrm{KL}$ is 8. How long is LM?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows rectangle JKLM with J at the upper left, K at the upper right, L at the lower right, and M at the lower left. The diagonal KM is drawn from M to K. A segment from J to an interior point N is drawn and is the angle bisector at J. Dashed perpendiculars indicate that N is 1 unit above LM and 8 units left of KL. Reasoning: Place coordinates as M=(0,0), L=(w,0), K=(w,h), and J=(0,h), so LM=w. Since N is 1 unit above LM and 8 units left of KL, N=(w-8,1). The diagonal KM has equation y=(h/w)x, so substituting N gives 1=h(w-8)/w, hence h=w/(w-8). The angle bisector at J of the right angle has slope -1, so its equation is y=h-x. Substituting N gives 1=h-(w-8), so h=w-7. Equating the two expressions for h gives w/(w-8)=w-7, so w=(w-7)(w-8). Expanding gives w^2-16w+56=0, whose roots are w=8±2√2. Since N is 8 units left of KL, w must be greater than 8, so w=8+2√2.

method.method_draft: Use analytic coordinates. From the diagram, place the rectangle with M=(0,0), L=(w,0), K=(w,h), and J=(0,h), so the requested length LM is w. The dashed perpendiculars and the text give that N is 1 unit above LM and 8 units left of KL, hence N=(w-8,1). Since N lies on diagonal KM, whose equation is y=(h/w)x, substitute N to get 1=h(w-8)/w. Since JN is the angle bisector of the right angle at J, in these coordinates its equation is y=h-x; substituting N gives 1=h-(w-8), or h=w-7. Equate h=w/(w-8) and h=w-7, solve (w-7)(w-8)=w, giving w=8±2√2. Because w must exceed 8, choose w=8+2√2.
